statement: Two-step sequence documented by three independent sources: the LFF held provisional FIFA membership from December 1991 (UEFA: readmitted 9 December 1991; LA Times: 'granted provisional membership in December') and was admitted (to full membership) at the FIFA Congress on 3 July 1992 (UPI and LA Times both report the Congress admissions; the FIFA report gives re-affiliation year 1992).
limitations: All three sources are non-FIFA; the exact semantics (what 'provisional membership' permitted in Dec 1991 - June 1992) is a policy question for the mainline, not decided here. Replaces the batch03 framing of AGB3-A006 as a bare conflict: the two dates are now documented as different steps of one sequence rather than rival claims for the same event.

statement: Namibia was among the 14 associations admitted at the FIFA Congress on 3 July 1992 (LA Times names Namibia explicitly; the FIFA report gives affiliation year 1992).
limitations: Wire report plus year-level FIFA record; not a FIFA primary document. All 5 target matches (1992-08-01 to 1992-12-19) postdate the documented admission day.

statement: The Cayman Islands was among the 14 associations admitted at the FIFA Congress on 3 July 1992 (LA Times names the Cayman Islands explicitly; the FIFA report gives affiliation year 1992).
limitations: Wire report plus year-level FIFA record; not a FIFA primary document. The single target match (1992-04-03) predates the documented admission day; provisional or earlier-effective status is not excluded by registered sources.

statement: The 14 associations admitted at the 3 July 1992 Congress are now fully identifiable from two independent contemporaneous reports: South Africa, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Russia, Armenia, Belarus, Georgia, Ukraine, Croatia, Slovenia, St. Kitts and Nevis (UPI) plus the Cayman Islands and Namibia (LA Times). North Macedonia is not among them (its 1994 admission year in the FIFA report stands without a day).
limitations: Both sources are wire reports, not FIFA documents; the identification relies on their mutual consistency (12+2 names) rather than an official list.
